qt: to the Commission Fredis Beleris (PPE) Subject:

The fishing sector across Europe is facing serious financial pressures due to high fuel prices. Fuel is one of the largest operating costs for fishing vessels, so rising fuel costs reduce fishers’ income, threaten the viability of fishing businesses and put jobs in coastal and island communities at risk. In April 2026, the Commission adopted the Middle East Crisis Temporary State Aid Framework (METSAF), allowing Member States to provide temporary support to the fishing sector, which is facing increased costs, until 31 December 2026. In parallel, the Commission has activated the crisis mechanism under the EMFAF, allowing Member States to compensate fishers for additional expenses and loss of income resulting from the crisis. In view of the above: 1.

Does the Commission intend to extend the operation of the METSAF and the EMFAF crisis mechanism and increase the limit of 50,000 per business, in order to ensure aid to fishers for the duration of the crisis?
Does the Commission intend to increase current funding, as the EMFAF funds available in the Member States have been exhausted or committed?
How is the sustainability of the sector ensured against new crises, since the proposal for fisheries funding in the new MFF 2028-2034 has been drastically reduced?
